articles.title: Oil prices edge higher after reported US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island, reviving supply concerns
articles.summary: Oil prices edged higher in early Asian trade on Tuesday after reports of a US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island raised fresh concerns about the conflict, even
articles.body: Oil prices edged higher in early Asian trade on Tuesday after reports of a US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island raised fresh concerns about the conflict, even as diplomatic efforts to end the war continued.Brent crude futures rose 48 cents, or 0.5%, to $105.25 a barrel by 0104 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude gained 47 cents, or 0.5%, to $96.93.The gains came a day after Brent slumped 7.63%, shedding $8.66 to settle at $104.77 a barrel, as markets weighed the possibility of progress in efforts to end the conflict.However, reports of fresh military action have put the focus back on the risk of further escalation. The Wall Street Journal reported, citing US officials, that American forces had struck Iran's Qeshm Island. Some officials described the strikes as defensive, intended to prevent Iran from targeting commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz.The waterway remains central to concerns over global energy supplies. Before the conflict began in late February, it carried around a fifth of the world's crude oil and natural gas. The sharp reduction in shipping traffic since then has kept supply risks elevated.At the same time, both sides have indicated that the door to negotiations remains open. Iran said contacts with Washington were continuing after talks with Qatari mediators ended without a breakthrough, although revised proposals were put forward.US President Donald Trump, meanwhile, cast doubt on whether he would resume threatened military strikes and said an agreement with Tehran was still possible. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian also said Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei had granted the government certain powers to pursue peace talks.The competing signals have left oil markets balancing the possibility of a diplomatic breakthrough against the threat of renewed military action. Brent had already climbed to a six-month high at the end of October amid concerns over an escalation in the Middle East.High fuel prices are also adding to pressure on Trump to bring the conflict to an end, with the war emerging as a key factor behind rising gasoline costs in the US.Separately, Washington is scheduled to host Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11 for discussions on ending the war in Ukraine, post-war security arrangements and de-escalation.You use AI every day. articles.title: FRRO network expands to 20 with new offices in Bhubaneswar, Kohima, Agartala
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Centre has notified three new foreigners regional registration offices (FRROs) — in Bhubaneswar, Kohima, Agartala, taking the total number
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Centre has notified three new foreigners regional registration offices (FRROs) — in Bhubaneswar, Kohima, Agartala, taking the total number of such offices to 20 in the country.Stating that the number of foreign visitors arriving for tourism, medical and educational purposes has witnessed a substantial rise, the home ministry in a statement said there is need to appoint FRROs in each state. “This will ensure service accessibility, enhance regulatory compliance and promote India as an attractive destination,” it said while reiterating home minister Amit Shah’s call for establishing FRROs in all state capitals by 2027.The FRRO monitors compliance with Indian immigration laws, handles cases of overstay and visa violations, and coordinates legal action or penalties where necessary.In the past couple of years, five new FRROs have become operational in Jaipur, Chandigarh, Aizawl (Mizoram), Amravati (Andhra Pradesh) and Guwahati.“Recently, three new FRRO offices, namely Kohima (Nagaland), Agartala (Tripura) and Bhubaneshwar (Odisha), have been notified. Earlier, Kohima and Agartala were under the jurisdiction of FRRO, Kolkata, whereas Bhubaneshwar was under the jurisdiction of FRRO, Hyderabad,” shared the MHA.The government is considering further increasing the FRRO network in the remaining states, namely Bihar, Goa, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur and Meghalaya.The 20 FRROs across the country are located at Ahmedabad, Amravati, Amritsar, Aizawl, Agartala, Bengaluru, Bhubaneswar, Calicut, Chennai, Cochin, Chandigarh, Delhi, Guwahati, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Kohima, Kozhikode, Lucknow, Mumbai and Trivandrum," the statement read.The expansion of the FRRO office network has a dual focus on facilitating foreigners' legitimate travel and stay in India and ensuring effective implementation of immigration laws and security requirements.You use AI every day. articles.title: Anthropic Q3 results: Revenue soars 1,127% to $17 billion, operating loss stands at $567 million
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence company Anthropic’s revenue surged 1,127 per cent year-on-year to $17 billion in the September quarter, but the rapid expansion
articles.body: Artificial intelligence company Anthropic’s revenue surged 1,127 per cent year-on-year to $17 billion in the September quarter, but the rapid expansion came with a sharp rise in computing costs, pushing the company into an operating loss.Anthropic reported an operating loss of $567 million for the three months ended September 30, compared with operating income of $974 million in the preceding quarter. Its updated registration statement, filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), showed that computing and infrastructure expenses jumped 382 per cent year-on-year to $9.9 billion, as quoted by ANI.The company attributed the pressure in part to the high cost of securing computing capacity through short-term commitments, which are more expensive than longer-term arrangements. It said it continues to face constraints in meeting demand.“We have consistently operated in a compute-constrained environment where customer demand exceeds available compute,” Anthropic said in the filing.The September-quarter operating loss also included around $2 billion in non-cash expenses linked to a donation-matching programme. On an adjusted basis, operating income stood at $2.5 billion, compared with $2.2 billion in the June quarter. Adjusted operating margin, however, narrowed to 15 per cent from 19 per cent.Anthropic expects its reliance on more expensive short-term computing arrangements to continue in the near term. “We expect our use of short-term compute to continue to increase in the near term,” it said, indicating that margins could remain under pressure as the company scales up to meet demand.For the first nine months of 2026, revenue reached $33.2 billion, against $2.5 billion in the corresponding period last year. Operating loss narrowed to $1.3 billion from $5.2 billion.The company reported a net loss of $23.3 billion for the September quarter and $104 billion for the first nine months of the year. Much of the nine-month loss was driven by a $94.3 billion non-cash charge arising from changes in the fair value of convertible notes and other financial instruments, primarily reflecting an increase in their valuation.Anthropic’s aggregate commitments to purchase and lease computing capacity stood at $895.4 billion, of which $447.5 billion is expected to fall due before December 2030. The scale of these obligations underscores the capital-intensive nature of building and operating advanced AI systems.Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI employees, Anthropic is seeking to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol ANT. The filing does not yet specify the number of shares to be offered or the price range. The proposed offering will include newly issued shares as well as shares held by existing shareholders.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: Gold price prediction today: Several global factors are likely to continue weighing on gold, making its upside limited, says Praveen Singh, Head Currencies and Commodities, Mirae Asset ShareKhan. Let’s take a look at his detailed view:Gold Performance: Spot gold prices, following a steep decline of over 3% in the week ending October 30, rose sharply on November 2 as crude oil prices slumped nearly 7% on hopes for resumption of peace talks between Iran and the US.In the week ending October 30, Spot gold fell 3.02% to $3875 as momentum selling gathered pace amid rising oil prices. At the time of writing this article on the night of November 2, the shiny metal was trading with a sharp gain of 2% at $3959.Geopolitics and oil: Oil prices slumped on Monday as Iran's Supreme leader Khamenei gave the government permission to hold peace talks amid heightened geopolitical concerns that US-Iran conflict can escalate violently. Earlier, Axios reported that Trump told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that he remains open to allowing more time for a diplomatic solution to the conflict with Iran. However, the situation remains uncertain as Iran continues to maintain the stance that it will facilitate energy transport through the Strait of Hormuz and return to formal negotiations only after the US lifts its economic blockade. At the time of writing this article on the night of November 2, Brent oil futures were trading at $105.77, down ~7% for the day and were at the lowest since October 16. Near-term support is seen around $103.50, followed by $100.Data roundup: US ISM manufacturing rose from 54.5 in September to 55.5 (forecast 54.50) in October -- highest since July, as the employment Index expanded for the fourth straight month. ISM prices paid edged lower from 77.90 to 75.2, vs the estimate of 77.20, but remains elevated. New orders rose for the ninth straight month. China's manufacturing PMI fell from 50.1 in September to 49.30 in October, as even non-manufacturing PMI contracted from 50.2 to 49.70. RatingDog manufacturing PMI edged lower from 52.1 in September to 52 in October, which was in line with the estimate. Euro-zone manufacturing PMI improved from 52.4 to 52.7 in its October final reading. UK's manufacturing PMI came in at 52.8 in October, which matched the forecast.Dollar Index and yields: Dollar Index eased 0.10% to 101.70 on Monday as oil prices slumped, though two-year US yields rose 2 bps to 4.6050, while tens were down 2 bps to 4.90%. Fed rate hike probability: Probability of the US Federal Reserve hiking the Fed fund rate stood at 77%, with total 2.35 hikes priced in by October 2027.US Midterm elections due on November 3:Democrats need a net gain of three seats to take control of the House and four seats to take control of the Senate. If the outcome goes down to the wire, the Associated Press may take days after the election to call control of the House, as was the case in the 2022 midterm elections, while calling control of the Senate could take even longer.Iran war and US elections: Even if the opposition gains control of Congress and takes office in January, this would not automatically bring an immediate end to the conflict. The President retains considerable authority as Commander-in-Chief to conduct ongoing military operations, while legislation compelling a withdrawal could face a presidential veto and require a two-thirds majority in both chambers to override it. However, an opposition-controlled Congress could increasingly constrain the administration through funding restrictions, war-related appropriations and aggressive congressional oversight. Thus, a change in congressional control would raise political pressure to de-escalate, but the conflict could persist amid a prolonged executive-legislative standoff.Gold ETF: Total known global gold ETF holdings stood at 100.97 Moz as of October 30, down 0.17 Moz for the week. Holdings are 2.02 Moz up YTD, though are up merely 0.02 Moz since the start of the Iran war on February 28. Holdings have fallen 0.58 Moz since the cycle high reached on October 21. COMEX inventory: Registered COMEX inventory at 14.81 Moz is down from the record peak of 24.25 Moz seen at the peak of tariff wars in April 2025. Inventories have risen from the cycle low of 14.19 Moz seen on August 7.CFTC positioning: Money managers reduced their net long gold bets by 1281 lots to 107,404 lots - the least bullish position in twenty weeks, according to the CFTC data for the week ending October 27. Likewise, long only positions fell 124 lots to 124,352 lots -- more than five-month low. Short-only positions were up 1157 lots to 16,948 lots-- two-week high. Fitch Ratings revised France’s outlook to negative:The rating Agency Fitch affirmed long-term issuer default rating at A+ but unexpectedly revised its credit outlook to negative on deterioration in public finances, high government debt, elevated borrowing costs, weaker growth and political uncertainty. Upcoming data: This week is crucial for financial markets as several key US data are on tap. Major data include September JOLTs job openings and final durable goods orders (November 3); October ADP employment change and ISM services (November 4); October nonfarm payrolls (November 6); and November preliminary University of Michigan sentiment and inflation expectations. Major focus will be on the nonfarm payroll report. Investors will monitor Eurozone and UK services and composite PMIs (November 4), and Eurozone October CPI inflation (November 4), too.Gold Price Outlook: High volatility in oil, and consequently gold, is likely as the US midterm elections approach. Geopolitical uncertainty remains elevated, with the US administration keeping both diplomatic and military options toward Iran open.The risk of renewed US-Israeli strikes on Iran after the elections remains significant. Even a Republican defeat in the midterms would not necessarily lead to an immediate de-escalation of the Iran conflict.Given the prevailing negative gold-oil correlation, near-term gold moves could remain highly sensitive to oil prices. A sustained decline in oil may require clearer signs of a diplomatic resolution to the Iran conflict.US nonfarm payrolls represent another major near-term catalyst for gold.Overall, gold's upside is likely to remain constrained unless prices decisively breach the 4,030-4,066 resistance zone. Supports are seen at 3,900/3,875/3,800/3,750. In the absence of a credible US-Iran agreement over the Strait of Hormuz, gold remains vulnerable to a test of the key $3,750 support. articles.title: IPO fundraising rises 30% to record Rs 84,400 crore in H1FY27: Report
articles.summary: India's mainboard IPO market witnessed a record fund mobilisation at Rs 84,400 crore in the first half of FY27, registering a 30 per cent rise over the
articles.body: India's mainboard IPO market witnessed a record fund mobilisation at Rs 84,400 crore in the first half of FY27, registering a 30 per cent rise over the year-ago period, with nearly 94 per cent of the funds raised during the July-September period, according to a report by Grant Thornton Bharat.As many as 71 companies made their stock market debut during April-September 2026, compared with 55 in the corresponding period a year ago.According to the report, the funds raised increased from Rs 64,900 crore in H1 FY26 to Rs 84,400 crore in H1 FY27.The average listing-day gains improved to 18 per cent from 10 per cent a year ago, while average retail oversubscription increased to 28 times from 25 times, the report titled 'India IPO Market: H1 FY27 and Q2 FY27 Review' said.Notably, September was the busiest month, with 32 IPOs collectively raising Rs 40,400 crore.In terms of sectoral contribution, financial services accounted for 43 per cent of the total capital mobilised during H1 FY27, while capital goods led in terms of the number of issues, with 15 IPOs.Domestic institutional investors (DIIs) emerged as an anchor to the equity market, recording net inflows of Rs 1.69 lakh crore during Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 13,900 crore from foreign portfolio investors (FPIs). This domestic investor support helped the market absorb a sharp rise in IPOs despite the NSE's benchmark index Nifty 50 declining 5.7 per cent in September."India's IPO market moved from caution to acceleration in Q2 FY27, helping deliver a record first half. While the scale of fundraising shows the market can absorb new issuance, investor demand stayed selective and increasingly focused on fundamentals, pricing, governance and the use of proceeds," Karan Marwah, Partner and Capital Markets Advisory Leader at Grant Thornton Bharat, said.The report noted that the IPO pipeline remained substantial, with 100 mainboard and 159 SME companies filing draft offer documents during H1 FY27.However, it cautioned that a large pipeline may not necessarily translate into completed listings, particularly in cases of regulatory approval lapses or incomplete market readiness.You use AI every day. articles.title: Elon Musk's next target: a major shake-up of America's wireless market
articles.summary: Elon Musk is looking to shake up America's wireless industry, potentially bringing the first major new competitive threat in years to a business dominated by...
articles.body:
Elon Musk is looking to shake up America's wireless industry, potentially bringing the first major new competitive threat in years to a business dominated by three companies.

Why it matters: The cellular industry has seen enormous technological change but relatively little disruption to its competitive structure. Musk has the money, spectrum and satellite network to attempt something different — though he faces daunting obstacles.

Driving the news: SpaceX is assembling the pieces to become a major U.S. wireless carrier, potentially building its own terrestrial network and buying available spectrum.

The moves are meant either to build the capability to bypass existing carriers or to bring them to the table for a deal that would allow Musk to strike a deal for wholesale access to their networks.

Musk may have reason to move quickly while the current administration and its regulatory appointees remain in place, a reason some analysts have cited in the context of proposals for a merger between Tesla and SpaceX .

What they're saying: Blair Levin, a former Federal Communications Commission chief of staff who now heads policy at Optimal Advisory, says Musk's financial resources distinguish him from previous challengers.

"For the first time, there is an entity capable of scaring investors in the traditional big three," Levin told Axios.

Unlike Dish, which faced serious financing constraints, SpaceX can draw on capital markets that have rewarded Musk's ambitious plans.

The latest: SpaceX has held talks with EchoStar about acquiring Boost Mobile or gaining access to its network arrangements, according to a Washington Post report Monday.

That could provide a quick route to customers and infrastructure, although approval of such a deal is far from a foregone conclusion if Musk's businesses are drawn into a regulator quagmire after the midterm elections.

The Post reported that Verizon, AT&T and T-Mobile have all rebuffed Musk's efforts to gain access to their networks.

State of play: Musk also has a path to maneuver around them.

SpaceX has agreed to multibillion-dollar spectrum deals , including a low-band variety useful for reaching customers indoors and supporting a traditional cellular network.

The company could build its own network using towers and smaller rooftop antennas, though doing so would require substantial investment and time.

The big picture: America's wireless industry has spent much of the past two decades consolidating.

T-Mobile once played the scrappy challenger, shaking up the industry with aggressive pricing and the elimination of unpopular practices.

But its 2020 acquisition of Sprint reduced the number of major nationwide carriers from four to three.

Regulators tried to preserve a fourth competitor by requiring the sale of Boost Mobile to Dish Network, which planned to build a nationwide network.

That effort never delivered the competitive alternative envisioned, leaving Verizon, AT&T and T-Mobile firmly entrenched.

articles.body: Across industries, a new generation of leaders is building on established foundations while rethinking how businesses grow, institutions evolve and communities benefit. From real estate and education to technology and leadership, their journeys reflect a shared focus on long-term value, meaningful progress and future-ready enterprises.Gulshan Estate Agents: Turning generational trust into the future of property advisorIn real estate, trust is built over decades, not transactions. That principle lies at the heart of Gulshan Estate Agents, founded in South Delhi in 1959, and now in its third generation of family leadership, with Geet Nayyar as Director, Legal and Finance. Bringing a contemporary lens to a legacy built on integrity, expertise and generational client relationships, Geet is strengthening the firm’s approach to property advisory.His focus lies in the less visible, but critical, dimensions of every transaction, due diligence, documentation and structuring. As South Delhi’s property landscape grows more complex, Geet’s vision is clear: evolve beyond conventional brokerage into comprehensive, credible advisory, while building a firm where reputation continues to compound across generations.Sardar Simarpreet Singh: Carrying a 25-year education legacy into its next chapter Director Sardar Simarpreet Singh, who has spent 12 years at JIS Group Educational Initiatives,is focused on carrying forward a 25-year legacy rooted in the belief that education should widen opportunity, not restrict it. What began as a family conviction about access to education has grown into a network serving 45,000 students1. Over the years, the group has expanded beyond engineering into management, university and medical education, while six of its colleges have received NAAC accreditation2. As the institution adapts to the needs of a changing generation, Singh’s focus remains on building on this legacy while staying true to the idea that shaped its beginnings.Dr. Irfan Khan: Building EBG Group into a future-ready enterpriseWith over two decades of entrepreneurial and leadership experience across electric mobility, wellness, hospitality, real estate, food and beverages, and consumer electronics, Dr. Irfan Khan has built his approach around sustainable growth and long-term value creation.As Founder and Chairman ofEBG Group, he is building a diversified business ecosystem guided by the philosophy of People, Planet and Progress.His vision focuses on transforming fragmented industries into scalable, professionally managed enterprises through strategic partnerships, joint ventures, franchising and asset-light business models.Believing that scale must be supported by strong systems, Dr. Khan prioritises operational discipline, technology integration, governance and leadership development.His ultimate ambition is to build an enduring institution that empowers entrepreneurs, strengthens brands and creates lasting enterprise value across generations, embodying EBG Group’s vision of Empowering a Better Globe.Syed Adil Husain: Scaling Technotask with AI + human support, technology and global expansioSyed has built Technotask around a customer-experience model that combines people, technology and AI. Keeping their focus on Tier-2 and Tier-3 India for service delivery, they have grown to more than 5,600 employees and 17+ centres, with operations extending to the UAE & Egypt. Technotask now works across 18+ industries while developing products in voice AI, conversation analytics and contact-centre technology to high volume Customer Experience Environments3. They have successfully deployed this model for several global clients, calling it AI + Human (Hybrid) Support. By reducing customer experience costs by up to 30%. Recently, NASSCOM BPM Confluence validated their approach towards CX and awarded them, under the category "Transforming Customer Experience"4.Siva Sankar and Atul Ghosh: Taking Spirulina Farming to India’s agricultural communitiesCousins Siva Sankar and Atul Ghosh came to spirulina from very different worlds.An NIT Calicut engineer and IIM Kozhikode alumnus, Sankar spent a decade building waste-to-value businesses through Noval Sustainability. In 2011, his algae-biofuel idea made Schneider Electric’s Top 100 Global Ideas.Ghosh brings 25 years of business experience across India, the Middle East, North Africa and the UK, from India’s first ATP tournament, the Tata Open, to global consumer brands.At Novalgae, they help farmers in drought-prone Ballari grow spirulina on their own land: a consistent income for rural families and a new weapon against malnutrition. In Sep 2026, IIMSAM named Novalgae its Constituent Technical and Research Partner.Venkatesh Gomatam: Rethinking how businesses choose their leadersVenkatesh Gomatam sees a leadership appointment as a decision about a business’s future, not simply its next vacancy. Drawing on over three decades across IHG, Accor and Hyatt, the Founder of The Fortitude Keystone brings an operator’s judgement to executive search and leadership advisory. The firm helps founders, boards and growing businesses clarify what leadership must deliver, then assess people beyond credentials for judgement, adaptability and the demands of the organisation. His focus extends beyond finding capable leaders to understanding the conditions in which they can succeed. The ambition: businesses whose leadership develops with their growth, rather than struggling to catch up.Reena Malik: Putting human connection at the heart of leadershipAfter more than 25 years in global leadership, Reena Malik has built her work around a question that often gets lost in corporate strategy: what makes people feel valued at work? A former partner at a Big Four firm and global head of people, she has led culture change and facilitated workshops across more than 35 countries5. Today, through Soul Hearted Consulting,she brings together emotional intelligence, organisational culture and leadership development to help businesses build human-centred, heart-centred workplaces where people feel safe to speak and be included. Her approach is grounded in a clear conviction: kindness, authenticity and integrity are not peripheral to leadership; they are what allow organisations to last.Raja Chellan: Shaping the next phase of EcowrkzRaja Chellan is steering Ecowrkz around the changing way businesses think about office space. The brand has developed a flexible workspace model spanning dedicated desks, private cabins, meeting rooms, virtual offices and other formats designed for teams at different stages of growth. With a strong presence across Chennai, along with branches in Coimbatore and Bengaluru, Ecowrkz is gradually widening its footprint while retaining a professionally managed approach to workspace infrastructure. Under this, Coworkseek allows operations to manage their coworking space. For Raja, the larger focus is on building a network that gives businesses the room to expand, contract or adapt without the rigidity that often comes with a conventional office setup.Swapnil Kale: Exploring Mumbai’s next real estate growth corridorSwapnil Kale, associated with PlotX Developers, is building a real estate investment proposition around emerging land markets and infrastructure-led growth. The company focuses on land opportunities across Pen, Uran, Panvel and Alibaug, connecting its offerings to the wider Mumbai 3.0 development story. The proposed KSC New Town, spanning 124 villages across Raigad district, represents a significant planned expansion of the Mumbai Metropolitan Region. articles.title: In some Senate battleground states, the cost of gas, groceries and housing are rising faster than the national average
articles.summary: From gas and groceries to housing and wage growth, midterm voters who are being squeezed by inflation say the economy is their top issue this Election Day.
articles.body: From gas and groceries to housing and wage growth, midterm voters who are being squeezed by inflation tell NBC News the economy is their top issue this Election Day. In 2024, President Donald Trump’s promise to bring down prices and make daily life more affordable helped him win back the White House. But nearly two years into his second term, Trump’s tariffs and his war with Iran have driven costs higher across the country, fueling deep discontent among voters. These frustrations aren’t confined to voters who support Democrats. More than half of Republicans, 53%, are dissatisfied with the state of the economy, according to the latest NBC News poll. Follow live updates on the midterm elections This has created an opening for Democrats to win majorities in both the House and the Senate. And while the House majority is widely expected to shift to Democrats after Tuesday night, the Senate is still very much a jump ball. Veteran election data analysts are quick to remind the public that as Tuesday’s voting and later counting unfolds, any one of the competitive Senate races could tip either way. Pain at the pump In several of the states with close Senate races, voters face gas prices that have climbed higher, and more sharply, than the mean nationwide prices over the same period. Across the country, the average cost of a gallon of gas has risen 40% since Feb. 28, the day Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu launched attacks on Iran that sent crude oil prices through the roof. Right before the war, the average price of unleaded was $2.98 per gallon, according to NBC News’ gas price tracker. On Monday, it was $4.16. In Iowa, however, the average price has climbed by significantly more, nearly 55% since late February. The same figure applies in Nebraska. In Kansas, gas prices are up by 53%. All three states broke for Trump in 2024. But two years later, they are in play, and Democratic Senate candidates Josh Turek in Iowa and Adam Hamilton in Kansas, as well as independent Dan Osborn in Nebraska, will be very closely watched Tuesday night. Drivers in Michigan are also experiencing an outsized jump, with gas up 51% from $2.99 in February to $4.52 Monday. There, Democrat Abdul El Sayed is facing off against Republican Mike Rogers. In Ohio, where Democratic former Sen. Sherrod Brown is challenging incumbent Republican Jon Husted, the price of a gallon of gas has climbed by 48%. “We aren’t going very many places,” Kathy DiCristofaro, of Youngstown, Ohio, told NBC News. “We’re retired and have had to cancel trips,” she said. In Maine, the price of a gallon of gas is 46% higher than it was before the war, creating a drag on Republican incumbent Sen. Susan Collins and an opportunity for Democrat Troy Jackson. Even when national average gas prices pivot lower, as they did throughout October, that doesn’t always extend to parts of the country where refinery activity influences fuel costs, particularly in the Great Lakes region. Far from the coasts, refineries that service Michigan, Ohio and Iowa cannot easily restore supply lost to weather events or refinery capacity. “When you’re isolated in the interior of the country, these problems can linger as long as the refinery is experiencing issues,” said Patrick De Haan, chief petroleum analyst at GasBuddy. Tariffs hit home Beyond the gas pump, voters are also feeling the sting of higher oil prices overseas in the form of increased transportation costs for groceries and retail goods. In several of the states with tight Senate races, average households are spending a lot more of their monthly income on groceries than shoppers elsewhere in the country, according to a WalletHub study. Among the 10 most cost-burdened cities for groceries in America, three of them are in Ohio: Cleveland, Toledo and Cincinnati. Also making the list are Detroit, and Hialeah, Florida, the latter a red state with surprisingly competitive gubernatorial and Senate races this year. “The cost of living is extremely high,” said Peris Morgan, a Michigan voter who spoke with NBC News outside a polling place in Sterling Heights on Monday. “Rent is high. Groceries are high, gas is high, everything is high, and so yeah, the cost of living compared to what people are being paid is not adding up.” While higher diesel costs have raised the price of transporting everyday goods, many businesses have also passed another big new cost on to consumers in the past two years: tariffs. Trump’s sweeping tariff regime has hit several of the states with major Senate races significantly harder than it has hit other states. The nonprofit National Taxpayers Union Foundation ranks all 50 states by how much tariffs have cost their economies since 2025. Three of the four states that pay the most for tariffs also have tight Senate races: Texas comes in second, Michigan third and Georgia is fourth. Further down the list, Florida, Ohio, North Carolina and South Carolina are all among the top 15. The lion’s share of these costs have come in the form of new import duties that affected the price of cars and trucks. But across the country, tariffs will cost every household an additional $1,100 this year, on average, according to estimates from the Yale Budget Lab. “This is not what we signed on for, for the tariffs and all this stuff,” said Jacqui Rose Tucker, a resident of Southwest Atlanta who spoke with NBC News’ Gabriella Rudy outside a grocery store. “My dollar does not go very far anymore,” she said, “This little bit of groceries was $218. It’s ridiculous. So yeah, I’m real concerned.” An unaffordable dream While daily costs are straining people’s wallets, longer-term investments like housing are also forcing voters to make sacrifices. In Alaska, the median home price in September was up by 4.0% year over year at $415,805, above the national average of $389,601 which was down 0.1%, according to data from Redfin. In Ohio, while median home prices are still below the national average, prospective buyers in September saw prices rise by 5.6% year over year across the state. States with tight Senate races are also overrepresented on Redfin’s list of cities where the price of a home has risen the most over the past year: In Akron, Ohio, average home prices are up 22% from last year, while in Cleveland they’ve risen by 13%. Joining Akron and Cleveland are Miami, metro Atlanta, Charleston, South Carolina and Cedar Rapids, Iowa — all in the top 10. As housing prices increase in many desirable metro areas, however, higher borrowing costs at the same time are putting homeownership out of reach for many younger voters, especially Gen Z and millennials. The average interest rate on a 30-year-fixed mortgage Monday was 7.27%. Your money buys you less While Americans are technically earning more in dollar terms on average, paychecks are not keeping up with the pace of inflation. Wages in September grew by 3.0% year over year. But the annual inflation rate hit 3.7%. Adjusting for inflation, this means average hourly earnings nationwide fell by about 0.7%. This disparity is another source of economic pressure on voters going into Election Day. But the gap between wage growth and inflation is significantly wider in some of the states that will be most closely watched Tuesday night. In Nebraska, purchasing power fell by 3.5% over the three months ending in August, relative to regional inflation. Iowa saw a drop of 2.6%. And in Alaska, real pay fell by 2.0% compared to the same period last year. “I work extraordinarily hard. I’m a single mom. I’ve got three kids,” said Jennie Larson, who planned to vote Tuesday morning in Iowa and spoke with NBC News in West Des Moines. “I go out to eat once a week, right? That’s like my one luxury. But outside of that, like the gas prices, the food prices, it’s unbelievable.”

articles.title: Stocks erase losses, oil tumbles after Trump says US will end $4 billion funding to Israel
articles.summary: By Niket Nishant and Gregor Stuart Hunter Nov 3 (Reuters) - Stocks in Europe and the US reversed course to trade higher on Tuesday as oil prices dropped afte...
articles.body:
By Niket Nishant and Gregor Stuart Hunter

Nov 3 (Reuters) - Stocks in Europe and the US reversed course to trade higher on Tuesday as oil prices dropped after US President Donald Trump said Washington ‌would stop $4 billion in funding to Israel after the end of this year.

Speaking to Fox News' Fox ‌and Friends, Trump said Israel no longer needed the funding. He had made a deal with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to stop the aid, ​he said.

The comments sent oil prices lower and helped stocks reverse their losses. The pan-European STOXX 600 index rose 0.13% to 650.3 points, while futures tracking the benchmark S&P 500 index added 0.14%.

The gains offered some relief after a fresh bout of AI anxiety unnerved investors, who are also on tenterhooks as voting began in crucial US ‌midterm elections.

Opinion polls show the Democrats are ⁠likely to take the House, while the Senate is too close to call. A sweep by Democrats could lead to tougher oversight of AI and more corporate regulation.

"In the case ⁠of a full blue sweep, I would expect some populist measures against AI. The narrative against data centres would get a tailwind," said Alexander Lis, chief investment officer at Social Discovery Ventures.

South Korea's KOSPI benchmark fell 3.6%, while Taiwan's index also dropped 3.6% ​for its ​steepest one-day decline since late July.

The dollar index, which measures ​the currency against a basket of peers, was ‌flat at 101.81. It hit a one-month low on Monday.

The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note rose 2.5 basis points to 4.9187%.

A surprise Republican sweep would likely lift yields and the dollar, said Steve Englander, co-head of FX research at Standard Chartered.

Brent crude futures fell 2.9% to $101.75 a barrel. Oil prices have whipsawed this week on conflicting signals from the US and Iran on ending the war in the Middle East.

"I don't think you could build a high conviction ‌view based on the Iran developments right now. And I think ​more investors should think the same way as I do," said Lis.

Apple on Monday forecast lower ​gross margins for the crucial holiday quarter, citing rising memory-chip costs, and projected services revenue ‌growth that fell well short of Wall Street expectations.

The ​iPhone maker's forecasts deepened the ​gloom in markets, which have been disappointed by lukewarm results from tech heavyweights.

Separately, the Chinese yuan weakened against the US dollar after the People's Bank of China said it would raise the foreign exchange reserve ratio, ​a move aimed at putting the brakes ‌on a long rally in the yuan.

Cryptocurrencies remained choppy after last week's Binance hack. Bitcoin nudged 0.5% higher ​to $77,110.83 and ether rose 1% to $2,278.10.

(Reporting by Niket Nishant in Bengaluru and Gregor Stuart Hunter in ​Singapore. Editing by Jamie Freed, Mark Potter and Jan Harvey)

articles.title: AMD to report Q3 results as chip stocks rebound following last week's steep selloff
articles.summary: AMD will report its third quarter earnings after the bell Tuesday.
articles.body:
AMD ( AMD ) will announce its third quarter results after the bell on Tuesday, as chip stocks stage a comeback after steep declines following Intel's ( INTC ) disappointing earnings last week.

AMD stock rose more than 4% in early trading on Tuesday.

While Intel reported better-than-anticipated Q3 results , it provided Q4 revenue estimates of between $15 billion and $16 billion, well below analysts' projections of $17 billion.

The news sent Intel stock plummeting nearly 29% .

The company blamed the outlook on a worse-than-anticipated decline in the PC market.

The industry is contending with two overlapping factors: difficult comparisons to last year, when Microsoft ended support for Windows 10, forcing enterprises to purchase newer Windows 11 systems, and the steady increase in PC prices, which is eating into demand.

While AMD generates the majority of its revenue via data center sales, a drop in PC demand would still hurt its bottom line.

For the third quarter, analysts anticipate AMD to report earnings per share of $1.97 on revenue of $13 billion, according to Bloomberg consensus estimates. The company saw EPS and revenue of $1.20 and $9.2 billion, respectively, in the same period last year.

AMD's Data Center arm is expected to see sales of $8.19 billion, an 88% increase from the $4.34 billion it reported last year.

The company's Client business revenue, which includes PC sales, is set to top $3.06 billion, up 11% year over year, but flat sequentially.

AMD's gaming business, however, could take a major hit, with Wall Street predicting a 49% revenue decline to $655 million.

The company's gaming division includes products ranging from PC graphics cards to custom silicon for game consoles. Both categories are facing higher prices due to the ongoing memory and storage shortage, depressing customer demand.

articles.title: California’s billionaire wealth tax is on the ballot: What to know about Prop 40
articles.summary: California voters will decide whether to approve Proposition 40, a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of the state's billionaires.
articles.body:
The California billionaire tax, Proposition 40, is finally coming to a vote on Tuesday. The measure would levy a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of the state's billionaires. Two competing initiatives on the same ballot, Props 41 and 42, are backed by opponents of the tax, including billionaires.

If either garners more yes votes than Prop 40, it could keep the tax from taking effect.

Early polls suggest support for the billionaire tax is slipping among California voters, according to reports.

The labor union Service Employees International Union-United Healthcare Workers West (SEIU-UHW) is spearheading the campaign for the tax on the state's ultra-wealthy to prevent hospital and clinic closures, protect healthcare jobs, and help fund K-14 public education and state food assistance programs.

Opponents, including Gov. Gavin Newsom, say the tax would fuel an exodus of wealthy company founders and investors, spark job losses, and further weaken California's economy.

Prop 40 would levy a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of billionaire state residents, subject to the asset restrictions noted below. Taxpayers could choose to pay the tax in five annual installments, with a 7.5% annual deferral charge on the unpaid balance.

Billionaire residents in California as of Jan. 1, 2026, would owe the tax in 2027. That's an estimated 255 eligible taxpayers, according to data from Altrata, a wealth-intelligence firm, reported by the Wall Street Journal.

The tax proposal is not based on income — that's a loophole that allows billionaires to pay less in income taxes than the average American . Rather, the proposed California tax is based on billionaires' assets, including equity holdings, often in their own companies. The impact on the most wealthy would vary widely.

A half-dozen or more high-profile billionaires relocated out of state as news of the proposed tax rolled out last year, so the number may be slightly lower.

Those who have reportedly relocated include Google co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin, though neither has said that their moves were related to the possible tax.

A Meta regulatory filing dated Oct. 21 said that founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg told a special board committee that he was considering moving out of the state to avoid the tax if it were passed.

The committee said it was "critically important to keep Mr. Zuckerberg in a leadership position with our Company and that he continue to reside in and manage the Company from our headquarters in California," and approved a special class of stock that he could use to pay any wealth tax due.

The tax's effect would vary widely. The Tax Foundation, a right-leaning tax policy nonprofit, projected that the tax would render Tony Xu, the founder of DoorDash, bankrupt, with a tax liability of $4.17 billion, unless he could challenge the initiative's valuation of his assets.

On the other hand, Jensen Huang of Nvidia would face a tax liability of more than twice that: $8.5 billion. He told Bloomberg that he's fine with that .

The California healthcare worker union, SEIU-UHW, launched the "emergency tax" initiative to offset possible healthcare staffing issues and service reductions at healthcare facilities. The union estimates a nearly $100 billion loss of federal funding over the next five years due to the passage of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

Taxpayers and trusts with assets over $1 billion would be taxed on businesses, securities, collectibles, and intellectual property, but the tax would exclude real property and certain retirement accounts and pensions.

The California Billionaire Tax Act is estimated to raise about $100 billion, according to the initiative's website. The Legislative Analyst's Office, the state's nonpartisan fiscal adviser, estimates that the state would collect tens of billions of dollars from the wealth tax but says the exact amount is harder to predict.

BillionaireTaxNow.org says the money would be used to:

Keep hospitals, ERs, clinics, nursing homes, and home care facilities open and staffed

"Stabilize" healthcare insurance premiums and coverage

Fund K-14 public education programs and staffing

Fund California food assistance programs

Arguments in favor of the California billionaire tax

The Institute on Taxation and Economic Policy, a left-leaning think tank, supports the California billionaire tax, saying that the One Big Beautiful Bill Act "cut health care and food support in part to pay for tax cuts for the very wealthiest Americans. The legislation gives more than $1 trillion in tax savings to the richest 1% of households over the next decade."

ITEP added in the analysis that, "ultra-wealthy households have many ways to enjoy a lavish lifestyle without selling most of their holdings, and so can largely avoid the individual income tax. The billionaire tax directly remedies this injustice by taxing all wealth, whether this wealth has been realized as income or not."

Arguments against the California billionaire tax

The Tax Foundation believes the California billionaire tax, as drafted, contains "aggressive design choices and possible drafting errors" that could result in the proposed one-time 5% tax being "dramatically higher."

It warns that "the poorly drafted initiative" could force company founders to sell "a significant portion" of their shares and lose their controlling interests. Stock prices could plunge, impacting retirement savings and investment account balances of working Americans.

The Hoover Institution, a right-leaning think tank, has said the wealth tax would leave California about $25 billion worse off, accounting for lost income tax revenue from billionaires leaving the state. It also estimated revenues from the levy would fall short of the $100 billion projection, more likely generating just $40 billion.

What about federal wealth tax proposals?

Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) has long advocated for a national wealth tax. His "Make Billionaires Pay Their Fair Share Act," co-sponsored by Rep. Ro Khanna (D-Calif.), was introduced in March.

The national tax would levy a 5% annual, not one-time, tax on the estimated 938 billionaires in the U.S., estimated to raise $4.4 trillion over the next 10 years. In the first year, the bill would give a $3,000 payment to "every man, woman, and child" in a household earning $150,000 or less.

The bill moved to committees in both the Senate and House, where no further action was taken.

Jeff Bezos's tax proposal: Some Americans should pay zero federal income tax

Jeff Bezos has turned the tables on the "tax the rich" effort. He is advocating for eliminating federal income taxes for lower-income Americans.

How billionaires get away with paying less income tax

From strategic investments to advanced planning, here's how the wealthy reduce their tax burden.

Mark Cuban has a challenge for CEOs: Give each worker a stake

Billionaire entrepreneur Mark Cuban says one way companies can help more people build wealth is by giving employees a stake in the businesses they help grow.

From capital gains strategies to charitable donations, here are some of the common tactics high earners use to shrink their tax bills.

How much does a millionaire actually owe the IRS on Tax Day?

Earning a $1 million salary puts you in the 37% tax bracket. Find out why many million-dollar earners pay taxes at a lower rate and how you could use their strategies to lower your tax bill.

What to know about the new (higher) SALT deduction — and how to claim it

The state and local tax (SALT) deduction jumped to $40,000 this tax year. See who qualifies, how the new cap works, and whether itemizing could boost your tax savings.

articles.title: ED action on Anil Ambani Group: 2 aircraft, other assets worth Rs 510 crore seized
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Tuesday attached assets worth Rs 510 crore including two private aircraft as part of its money laundering
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Tuesday attached assets worth Rs 510 crore including two private aircraft as part of its money laundering investigation into alleged bank fraud involving the Reliance Anil Ambani Group (RAAG).The agency said the action was linked to alleged fraud involving Reliance Home Finance Ltd (RHFL) and Reliance Commercial Finance Ltd (RCFL), amounting to Rs 263.05 crore, and Reliance Communications Ltd (RCOM), involving Rs 247.12 crore.The ED has issued a provisional attachment order under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), covering properties worth Rs 510 crore.In the RCOM case, the attached assets include two chartered aircraft, six land parcels and an office premises in Maharashtra, the ED said in a statement.The two aircraft are a Dassault Falcon 2000 and an Embraer.In the RHFL and RCFL case, the agency has attached two windmills in Tamil Nadu, along with bank balances, fixed deposits and investments.The agency claimed its investigation found that the group had siphoned off public funds from banks and financial institutions, misused the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) to ring-fence corporate assets for personal use, and diverted funds from India to offshore tax havens.“A large part was utilised for the individual benefit of the promoters and their family,” the ED alleged, PTI reported.The agency said it has arrested 10 people in the cases and filed six chargesheets. It has also launched a separate investigation under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA).With the latest attachment, the total value of assets attached and seized in the cases has reached Rs 23,100 crore, according to the ED.You use AI every day. articles.title: Chip stocks are bouncing back from a fresh bear market as Wall Street's safe havens slip
articles.summary: The chip sell-off is reversing as Apple, staples and utilities slide, with AMD earnings and the midterm elections up next.
articles.body:
Monday's close left chip stocks in a fresh bear market, below their summer lows and a key technical level. Tuesday, they're bouncing back like they want to make the bears regret it.

The PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) finished Nov. 2 about 22% below its Oct. 6 high, its second bear market since June. It was also the index's second straight close below its 200-day moving average , a line it hadn't closed under since June 2025, and its lowest close since April.

Nearly every chip and storage stock in the S&P 500 rose in early trading Tuesday, led by memory and chip-equipment names, and the index climbed back above its July 29 low. If chips can hold that ground, Monday's breakdown starts to look like a bear trap — a break below a key level that quickly reverses, catching traders who bet on more losses.

The bigger hurdle sits just overhead. The iShares Semiconductor ETF ( SOXX ) needs to get back above its 200-day average, near $477, to start repairing the damage. Above that, the next levels to watch are about $524 and $596.

Chip stocks have climbed in all eight midterm cycles since 1994, measured from the last October close through the following June, by Yahoo Finance calculations. That's the stretch Stock Trader's Almanac editor Jeff Hirsch calls the best months of the year for semiconductors . But in 2002 and 2018, chips first fell about another 11% before the rally kicked in.

Election Day itself has been kind to stocks too. The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) has risen on 10 of the last 14 midterm election days, going back to 1970.

Meanwhile, the rest of the market is moving the other way. Roughly two-thirds of S&P 500 stocks fell in early trading, a mirror image of Monday, when about 7 in 10 rose while chips sank. Consumer staples, utilities, and real estate, the safe havens that carried the market through October, slipped.

From the Oct. 6 close through Nov. 2, staples and health care climbed about 10% to 11%, while SOXX fell 23%.

Apple ( AAPL ), which has become Wall Street's hedge against the AI trade , saw its shares fall after it warned that memory costs will keep rising. Luke Kawa, head of markets at Sherwood News, called the seesaw between Apple and chips "almost Pavlovian."

"Apple goes down and what goes up in response? Semis," Kawa told Yahoo Finance on Nov. 3.

He also sees real damage in the charts. "What seems different this time is that it's really the first time throughout the AI boom that we're now seeing … lower highs and lower lows across major swaths of the space," Kawa said. Lower highs and lower lows are the very definition of a downtrend.

articles.title: Binance says hackers used fake job interview to compromise computer before $6.3 billion attack
articles.summary: Binance said hackers used a bogus job interview to breach a computer and gain control ​over the company’s wallets before draining $6.3 billion worth of crypto.
articles.body: Binance said on Tuesday hackers used a bogus job interview to compromise a computer and an internal artificial intelligence tool to gain control ​over the company’s wallets before draining $6.3 billion worth of crypto, in what could ‌be the largest-ever financial heist. In a initial report into what went wrong, the world’s largest crypto exchange detailed a sophisticated hacking endeavour that began with an advertisement for a tampered version of a ​coding tool in June and set in chain a series of security breaches ​that culminated in the theft of the crypto on October 29. The ⁠FBI has blamed a North Korean hacking group, a claim North Korea has rejected. Binance ​has said it is repaying all customers who have lost funds through the hack. Binance said ​that the attack started when an employee from its wallet developer team in June downloaded an AI tool that had been tampered with. The crypto exchange detected this, replaced the device and changed credentials ​but the employee’s role and that of others on the wallet team were exposed ​to the hacker. Then in September a second software engineer seeking a new job downloaded “malicious code repository” onto ‌his ⁠computer after interviewing for what the person thought was a legitimate role, including meeting virtually with the CEO of a fictitious company. On Oct. 20, the attacker used the compromised computer plus an internal AI tool to gain control of the wallet developer’s system and ​that of a second ​wallet developer on ⁠that team. On Oct. 29 the attacker used the second wallet developer’s computer, using stolen credentials from the first wallet developer, and triggered ​a malicious script to launch the attack. “This should not have ​happened, and ⁠we apologise for the concern, disruption and uncertainty it caused our users, partners and the wider industry,” Binance said in the report. As a result of the hack, Binance is ​increasing investments in AI-enabled detection and is working on ​establishing a security research fund and targeted initiatives with leading AI companies.
